title: Functions Input and Output Bindings
description: Learn how to use Azure Functions bindings to connect your functions to Azure services without writing boilerplate connection code.

data.text: Bindings are a declarative way to connect your function to other services. Instead of writing connection code for every Azure service, you use attributes that automatically handle input and output.
A function can have multiple input and output bindings but only one trigger.

items: Input binding — reads data from an external service into your function parameter
Output binding — writes data from your function result to an external service
Trigger binding — is also an input binding (provides the event payload)

data.title: C# — Blob Input and Queue Output Bindings
Connection Strings in local.settings.json
data.text: Store connection strings in the `Values` section of local.settings.json. Never commit this file to source control. In Azure, configure the same settings in the Application Settings of the Function App.

Bindings are configured through attributes in code and through the `host.json` file for global settings. The `Connection` property points to an app setting name that holds the actual connection string.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Bindings connect functions to external services declaratively
Input bindings bring data in; output bindings send data out
Each function has one trigger but multiple bindings
Connection strings are stored in app settings
data.takeaway: Bindings eliminate boilerplate connection code for Azure services.
